'''NMDC Limited''', formerly '''National Mineral Development Corporation''', is an Indian [[Public sector undertakings in India|public sector undertaking]] involved in the exploration of [[iron ore]], [[rock phosphate|rock]], [[gypsum]], [[magnesite]], [[diamond]], [[tin]], [[tungsten]], [[graphite]], [[coal]] etc. It is India's largest iron ore producer and exporter, producing more than 45 million tonnes of iron ore from three mechanized mines in [[Chhattisgarh]] and [[Karnataka]]. It also operates the only mechanized diamond mine in the country at [[Panna, India|Panna]] in [[Madhya Pradesh]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Law |first=Abhishek |date=2024-09-26 |title=NMDC Ltd eyes lithium block acquisition in Australia & Africa |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/nmdc-eyes-lithium-block-acquisition-in-australia-africa/article68686156.ece |access-date=2024-10-24 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}}</ref>

==Operating mines==
* Bailadila Iron Ore Mine, Kirandul Complex, South Bastar district, Dantewada (C.G.)Steel<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2024 |title=66th Annual Report 2023–2024 |url=https://www.nmdc.co.in/cms-admin/Upload/Annual_Report_Documents/96b25296b81b4abdbcddba9f5276f457_20241017201802710.pdf |website=nmdc.co.in}}</ref>
* Bailadila Iron Ore Mine, Bacheli Complex, South Bastar district, Dantewada (C.G.)
* Donimalai Iron Ore Mine, Donimalai, [[Bellary district, Karnataka]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bhattacharya |first1=Prasenjit |title=India's NMDC gets nod to expand iron ore Mine |url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en/news/2037427-indias-nmdc-gets-nod-to-expand-iron-ore-mine |access-date=31 March 2020 |agency=Argus Media |date=19 December 2019}}</ref>
* Kumarswamy Iron Ore Mine, Bellary District, Karnataka
* Diamond Mining Project, Majhgawan, Panna (M.P.)<ref name=":0" />

NMDC Ltd. is diversified into other raw materials for the steel industry such as low silica limestone. Production of [[Magnesite#Uses|dead burnt magnesite]] and further value addition is under study through its subsidiary J K Mineral Development Corporation Limited.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-03-14 |title=Amitava Mukherjee assumes additional charge as NMDC CMD |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/amitava-mukherjee-assumes-additional-charge-as-nmdc-cmd/articleshow/98636198.cms |access-date=2025-12-31 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

NMDC Ltd. has taken over a silica sand mining and [[beneficiation]] project from Uttar Pradesh State Mineral Development Corporation Ltd. The plant is designed to produce beneficiated high purity silica sand to a capacity of 300,000 tonnes per year as the raw material for production of float/sheet glass.

A memorandum of understanding has been signed between NMDC, [[Indian Rare Earths Limited]], (IREL) and Andhra Pradesh Mineral Development Corporation to establish a joint venture for the development of Bheemunipatnam Beach Sand. The project envisages mining of beach sands, setting up of [[mineral separation plant]] for [[ilmenite]] concentrate and a downstream value addition plant for conversion of ilmenite into [[rutile#Synthetic rutile|synthetic rutile]]/TiO<sub>2</sub> slag/TiO<sub>2</sub> pigment with [[pig iron]] as by-product.

==NMDC Steel Limited       ==
NMDC set up a 3 MTPA capacity greenfield [[Nagarnar Steel Plant]] based on HiSmelt technology, 16 km from [[Jagdalpur]] in [[Chhattisgarh]] state, with an estimated outlay of Rs 20000 crore.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.projectsinfo.in/News.aspx?nId=7dnGsGVKFCkeGmlJyFhljw== |title=Archived copy |website=www.projectsinfo.in |access-date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202195512/http://www.projectsinfo.in/News.aspx?nId=7dnGsGVKFCkeGmlJyFhljw== |archive-date=2 February 2022 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

A pure-play miner, NMDC had in 2009–10 conceived the Nagarnar steel plant with the intention of moving up the value chain and diversifying its portfolio. The idea was also to hedge itself against the vagaries of iron ore prices.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.financialexpress.com/economy/nmdc-steel-unit-divestment-govt-firm-despite-chhatisgarh-cm-warning/645395/| title=NMDC aims September start for Nagarnar steel mill| website=FE| date=28 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Mohanty |first1=Meera |title=Steel ministry wants to put off sale of NMDC's Chhattisgarh steel plant |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/steel/steel-ministry-wants-to-put-off-sale-of-nmdcs-chhattisgarh-steel-plant/articleshow/71381533.cms |access-date=31 March 2020 |work=The Economic Times |date=1 October 2019}}</ref>

The plant site is around 16 km from Jagdalpur and 6 km from the Odisha–Chattishgarh border. The nearest railway station is Amaguda (around 2 km). The site is located on [[National Highway (India)|National Highway]] [[National Highway 30 (India)|NH 30]]. 
The nearby airports are Jagdalpur, [[Raipur]] & [[Vishakhapatnam]] and the nearest seaport is Visakhapatnam located at a distance of approx 325 km. The nearest river is [[Indravati River|Indravati]], located at a distance of 3 km.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nmdc.co.in/right_pplant/Brochure%20circulated%20in%20EOI%20Conference-31.05.11.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=21 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120502185439/http://www.nmdc.co.in/right_pplant/Brochure%20circulated%20in%20EOI%20Conference-31.05.11.pdf |archive-date=2 May 2012 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

In 2023 NMDC Steel became a publicly traded company on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and [[National Stock Exchange of India]], after a demerger from NMDC in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-28 |title=NMDC shares trade ex-demerger. Should you buy? |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/nmdc-shares-trade-ex-demerger-of-steel-business-edelweiss-has-buy-tag-11666937426454.html |access-date=2023-04-20 |website=Mint |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=20 February 2023 |title=NMDC Steel makes market debut at Rs 30.25 |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/stocks/nmdc-steel-makes-market-debut-at-rs-30-25-10123101.html |access-date=2023-04-20 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en}}</ref>

== Listings and shareholding ==
The equity shares of NMDC are listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India.

As of February 2020, the [[Government of India]] held a 69.65% equity in NMDC.<ref>{{cite news |title=Govt of India cuts stake in NMDC by 2.63% |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/govt-of-india-cuts-stake-in-nmdc-by-2-63-120021100984_1.html |access-date=1 April 2020 |work=Business Standard|location=New Delhi |date=11 February 2020}}</ref> 225,339 individual shareholders hold approximately 3.79% of its shares. The balance is held by insurance companies (14.31%), foreign institutional investors (5.78%), [[mutual funds]] (4.42%), and banks (1.96%). [[Life Insurance Corporation of India]] is the largest non-promoter shareholder in the company with a 13.699% shareholding.<ref>{{cite web |date=30 December 2022 |title=Intimation under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 made on 30th December, 2022 |url=https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/d7d2e6f2-9bf9-4bd5-b3ce-1444f80da7c6.pdf |access-date= |publisher= |location=}}</ref>

== International ==
[[File:National Mineral Development Corporation 2017 stamp of India.jpg|thumb|upright=1.4|A 2017 stamp dedicated to the 60th anniversary of the National Mineral Development Corporation]]
In [[Australia]], Legacy Iron Ore, a majority-owned NMDC company, holds majority stakes in gold and iron ore projects in [[Western Australia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nmdc.co.in/CMD/Default.aspx|title=NMDC Limited – Our CMD|website=www.nmdc.co.in|access-date=7 October 2017}}</ref> In 2023, NMDC started exploring for Lithium reserves in the company's, majority owned, Mount Bevan mine in Australia.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Arora |first=Neha |date=2023-04-19 |title=Iron ore miner NMDC exploring lithium reserves for mining in Australia |url=https://theprint.in/india/indias-nmdc-explores-lithium-reserves-for-mining-in-australia/1527403/ |access-date=2023-04-20 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref>

NMDC Limited was awarded the Corporate Social Responsibility Award Global Metals Award 2018 in the Corporate Social Responsibility category in London, the first time since inception that an Indian company received the award.<ref>{{cite web |title=Congratulations to the winners of the 2018 Platts Global Metals Awards! |url=https://gma.platts.com/Winners/Winners2018 |website=S&P Global Platts |access-date=31 March 2020 |location=London}}</ref>
